cases.expectation: GET /api/settings/failover returns the stored pair; heartbeat test does a real TCP connect; the canonical surface answers: GET /api/ha/status (200, healthy with both nodes up), GET /api/settings/ha (200, canonical settings), GET /api/ha/decisions (200, array), and POST /api/ha/heartbeat answers 401 without the peer secret.

cases.title: Standby killed -> primary reports degraded/unavailable, no false promotion
cases.expectation: With the standby process dead, the primary heartbeat test must report unreachable, the primary must surface the failure in GET /api/ha/status (degraded while the peer row is within grace, unavailable once past it — the canonical service counts registered peers, not itself), the primary must stay up, and nothing may promote.

cases.title: Primary killed -> standby promotes with a real decision record (exact timestamps)
cases.expectation: With the primary process dead, the standby must promote itself to primary and record the decision (when, why, gapMs) in GET /api/ha/decisions. Canonical grace is heartbeatSec(5) x missThreshold(3) = 15s from the last heartbeat, so the harness polls up to 45s for the promotion.

cases.title: Primary returns -> re-registration demotes the promoted standby, no dual-primary
cases.expectation: After the primary restarts, exactly one node may report role primary. The returning primary re-registers (POST /api/ha/register on boot); the promoted standby demotes on that handshake and records an ha.demote (primary-rejoined) decision. A second primary is a split-brain bug.

cases.title: Stale heartbeat (old sentAt) -> rejected 400 stale_heartbeat, fresh accepted
cases.expectation: A canonical heartbeat carrying sentAt 24h old must be rejected (400 stale_heartbeat), never treated as a live heartbeat; the same heartbeat with a fresh sentAt must be accepted (200).
